detections.summary: A hidden cross-origin iframe was inserted after load.

alternativeExplanations: A viewability, verification or cookie-sync frame inserted by an ordinary ad.
A consent or login helper frame.
detections.confidenceRationale: A hidden cross-origin frame was observed, but no ad-selection request preceded it in the same frame lineage, and such frames are common in ordinary advertising.

evidence.observed: The page sensor observed a hidden cross-origin iframe targeting ib.adnxs.com inserted 3157 ms after the frame loaded in a frame on ads.pubmatic.com.

limitations: Page signals come from an opt-in content script in sub-frames and report structural facts only (element kind, size class, target hostname); page text, cookie values and full URLs are never collected.
A hostile page can suppress or imitate these DOM signals; absence of a signal is not evidence that nothing happened, and a signal alone does not show what the inserted element did.
missingVisibility: What code actually executed inside the page, and its effect on the device, is not observed; only network metadata and, where enabled, bounded analysis of selected response text are available.

detections.ruleName: Hidden cross-origin iframe inserted after load
detections.significance: In the documented chain, selected devices received code that inserted a 1x1 frame to load the next stage. A hidden frame alone is common; together with a preceding ad-selection request it matches that step.
detections.summary: A hidden cross-origin iframe was inserted after load.

alternativeExplanations: A viewability, verification or cookie-sync frame inserted by an ordinary ad.
A consent or login helper frame.
detections.confidenceRationale: A hidden cross-origin frame was observed, but no ad-selection request preceded it in the same frame lineage, and such frames are common in ordinary advertising.

evidence.observed: The page sensor observed a hidden cross-origin iframe targeting secure-assets.rubiconproject.com inserted 5 ms after the frame loaded in a frame on cs-tam.yellowblue.io.

limitations: Page signals come from an opt-in content script in sub-frames and report structural facts only (element kind, size class, target hostname); page text, cookie values and full URLs are never collected.
A hostile page can suppress or imitate these DOM signals; absence of a signal is not evidence that nothing happened, and a signal alone does not show what the inserted element did.
missingVisibility: What code actually executed inside the page, and its effect on the device, is not observed; only network metadata and, where enabled, bounded analysis of selected response text are available.
recommendedActions: Review the listed events and the cited research before drawing conclusions.
If you have reason to believe you are personally targeted, seek help from a digital-security helpline (for example Access Now's Digital Security Helpline) rather than acting on this alert alone.

detections.summary: A hidden cross-origin iframe was inserted after load.

alternativeExplanations: A viewability, verification or cookie-sync frame inserted by an ordinary ad.
A consent or login helper frame.
detections.confidenceRationale: A hidden cross-origin frame was observed, but no ad-selection request preceded it in the same frame lineage, and such frames are common in ordinary advertising.

evidence.observed: The page sensor observed a hidden cross-origin iframe targeting cs.admanmedia.com inserted 189 ms after the frame loaded in a frame on cs.seedtag.com.

limitations: Page signals come from an opt-in content script in sub-frames and report structural facts only (element kind, size class, target hostname); page text, cookie values and full URLs are never collected.

missingVisibility: What code actually executed inside the page, and its effect on the device, is not observed; only network metadata and, where enabled, bounded analysis of selected response text are available.

alternativeExplanations: A viewability, verification or cookie-sync frame inserted by an ordinary ad.
A consent or login helper frame.
detections.confidenceRationale: A hidden cross-origin frame was observed, but no ad-selection request preceded it in the same frame lineage, and such frames are common in ordinary advertising.

evidence.observed: The page sensor observed a hidden cross-origin iframe targeting eus.rubiconproject.com inserted 4 ms after the frame loaded in a frame on cs.pgammedia.com.

limitations: Page signals come from an opt-in content script in sub-frames and report structural facts only (element kind, size class, target hostname); page text, cookie values and full URLs are never collected.
A hostile page can suppress or imitate these DOM signals; absence of a signal is not evidence that nothing happened, and a signal alone does not show what the inserted element did.
missingVisibility: What code actually executed inside the page, and its effect on the device, is not observed; only network metadata and, where enabled, bounded analysis of selected response text are available.
recommendedActions: Review the listed events and the cited research before drawing conclusions.
If you have reason to believe you are personally targeted, seek help from a digital-security helpline (for example Access Now's Digital Security Helpline) rather than acting on this alert alone.

redaction.note: Default profile: sensitive values are never recorded; hostnames are shown as observed.
redactedFields: cookie values and request or response headers
full urls (replaced by host, path pattern and parameter names)
path segments that look like tokens or identifiers

visibilityLimitations: A browser extension cannot inspect the device itself, so it cannot detect installed spyware, operating-system compromise, or exploits delivered outside the browser.
A browser extension cannot see network traffic outside the browser, such as other applications, DNS lookups, or device-level connections.
Encrypted content is visible only where the browser exposes it to the extension; requests blocked by other extensions or the browser may not be observed.
Indicator sets describe documented infrastructure as of their published date and are not exhaustive.
